messages.subject: biogeographical stochastic mapping question
parts:
This addresses a question about the relationship between the y, s, v, and j parameter values, and the event counts that you will get from biogeographical stochastic mapping.

This is part 1/2...

From: Nick Matzke <mat...@nimbios.org>
Date: Mon, Sep 15, 2014 at 7:09 PM
Subject: Re: biogeographical stochastic mapping
To: dspa...@wisc.edu


Hi Daniel!  

Glad you were able to get stochastic mapping working!

I don't remember the event types being numbered -- perhaps your settings are reading the event types as factors, and then some other function is converting the factors to numbers.  If you do:

options(stringsasfactors = FALSE)

...at the beginning of an R session, that should turn the factors silliness off.

In any case, I usually order things y, s, v, j (sympatry, subset sympatry, vicariance, jump dispersal), so you're probably close.

I suspect your j counts and your ML estimate of j actually aren't in conflict.  Remember, y,s,v, and j are per-event weights. The conditional probabilities of each cladogenesis event, given an ancestral range, are 

(weight of a particular individual event, e.g. AB->A,B) / (total weight of all cladogenesis events starting from AB)

So, if your ML j in DEC+J equals 0.1124, the per-event weights of y, s, and v are each (3-j)/3 = ~0.96.  So by default you'd expect a particular j event to be about 1/8 as common as a particular y, s, or v event, which is very roughly what you see in your stochastic map counts.

The ACTUAL counts will be influenced by the tip data and the state space.  The relative numbers of possible y,s,v, and j events differ depending on how many areas, maximum range size, etc., there are. See Table 1 of Matzke 2014 to "get" this -- I attach the page proofs which are easier to read than the early-access word doc.

I can't say for sure if this applies for your data, but typically, if you have hundreds of species and 9 areas, and if (as is typical) many species are single-area endemics and there are many clades all sharing a single area, then the most common event at cladogenesis is sympatry: A->A,A, or B->B,B, etc.  *If* this is the case, then it may be that 90% or whatever of your nodes need nothing but sympatry events.  When ysv  and j are being estimated, then, the main thing is that y has to be way bigger than j to maximize the data likelihood.  Because y=s=v under DEC+J (and DEC), this forces s and v to also be high like y is, even if v and s are unnecessary.  

(Is this is a peculiar feature of DEC-type models?  Yes it is. Does this mean there are better models out there?  Almost certainly.  Why didn't I make even more models immediately?  The DEC+J thing by itself was surprising enough to people, and especially reviewers, that I have decided to let that one sink in for a bit, just to get people used to model selection in biogeography.)

Cheers!
Nick




On Mon, Sep 15, 2014 at 5:28 PM, Daniel Spalink <dspa...@wisc.edu> wrote:
Dear Nick,


Thanks for having such a thorough wiki page and example scripts for BioGeoBEARS!


I have been using the stochastic mapping scripts that you provided on your wiki and Google groups pages, hoping to ultimately get a sense of the probability of the various cladogenetic event types (given my tree, data, and model). Adding J to DEC significantly improves the likelihood of the model (p=9.7e-19) for my dataset, which includes a few hundred tips and 9 areas for a clade with a cosmopolitan distribution.


I’m in the process of generating 100 stochastic maps and counting each of the values in the clado_event_type column. I have been assuming that 1 = sympatry, 2 = vicariance, 3 = subset sympatry, and 4 = jump dispersal. Looking at my results so far I am surprised that jump dispersals only make up about 5% of all cladogenetic events. Given how much the model was improved by adding J, I suppose I expected jump dispersals to play a larger role. Am I perhaps interpreting my results incorrectly, or misunderstanding a more fundamental concept?


I’ve attached my results and the script I have been using. I much appreciate any help you can give, and please let me know if you need more information.


Many thanks,


Daniel
